latency.note: retrieval and paper ranking only; generation latency is measured separately because it depends on the provider

faiss.note: score differences of ~1e-7 are float32-versus-float64 rounding; order can differ only between near-tied vectors

clustering.caveat: Silhouette is measured on the original embedding space but the clusters were found in a 2-D UMAP projection, which is not optimised for it, so low values are expected. With few clusters it mostly reflects one split; a largest-cluster share near 1 means the map found one topic, not sub-topics. Judge cluster quality by reading the labels.

graph.note: precision of OpenAlex edges against the PDFs' own reference lists; an unmatched edge may be a title formatted differently in the reference list, not a wrong edge

retrieval.judged_by: Claude (an AI model), PROVISIONAL. Judged from each candidate's title and the first ~210 characters of its abstract, blind to which retriever returned it. Rubric: relevant if a researcher searching the query would want to read the paper because it substantially addresses the query topic; passing mentions (e.g. 'RAG reduces hallucination' as background) do not count. This is NOT a human judgement and has not been checked by the project owner - replace or review before presenting.
retrieval.caveat: Relevance is judged over the pooled top results of these same four modes, so a relevant paper none of them retrieved is invisible to every metric (pooling bias). Recall is therefore recall within the pool, not recall over the whole literature.

tau.note: RRF scores are rank-based (a question whose BM25 and dense top results coincide scores exactly 2/61 however weak the match), so calibrate on dense cosine or BM25

retrieval_bootstrap.method: paired bootstrap over queries, 5000 resamples, 95% interval of the mean difference

refusal_end_to_end.label_correction_on_inspection: 1 question labelled unanswerable ('How do transformers implement multi-head self-attention?') was ANSWERED with 2 citations to real passages in the collection that describe it; the label was wrong, not the system. Corrected accuracy 39/40.
refusal_end_to_end.score_threshold_alone: best dense-cosine threshold 0.7755 gives F1 0.87 (precision 0.91, recall 0.83): it would falsely refuse ~17% of answerable questions, so it does not beat the model's own refusal
refusal_end_to_end.decision: REFUSAL_TAU stays unset; the model's INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT refusal plus 'no retrieval hits' and 'no valid citation' are the active refusals
